subject: Request: per-account evaluation hooks & prompt-template ops for CoreBank POC
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Request: per-account evaluation hooks & prompt-template ops for CoreBank POC

Team —

Quick ask on behalf of CoreBank (DEAL-8841): they're in a two-week POC and require a way to run their evaluation prompt templates against a small, customer-provided eval set prior to rolling an updated prompt into production. The ask is twofold:

1) A per-account "eval hook" that can take a JSONL eval-set and run a small batch evaluation pipeline (accuracy/QA checks) when we promote a prompt change. Output should be stored in a customer-visible artifact (drive link or S3).

2) A lightweight ops API to attach/select prompt-templates at the account level (so they can stage multiple prompt variants and promote one to default for their traffic).

Why this matters: CoreBank is asking for this as a gating requirement for deployment — if we can't demonstrate controlled evaluation and a safe promotion path they will require a longer security review and may pull back on the commitment. Conservative ARR estimate for the expansion is $1.2M ARR.

Resources I can provide: their NDA (attached), a small eval-set (attached), and a CoreBank engineer on standby for integration questions.

Asks for you: can product/eng give a brief feasibility note and an ETA for a minimally viable implementation (we're looking for something we can ship as a canary for the POC within 2 weeks)? If there are security/ops blockers, call those out explicitly so I can push the right artifacts from CoreBank.

Thanks — I put this as P1 for the POC.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: CoreBank_MVP_requirements.pdf, corebank_sample_eval_set.jsonl

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-21T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: per-account evaluation hooks & prompt-template ops for CoreBank POC

Monica —

Thanks for the clear ask and attachments. High-level thoughts: conceptually this is sensible and aligns with our "Reduce regression risk for enterprise prompts" initiative. There are two implementation options that differ by risk/cost:

A) Fast path (2 weeks): build an orchestration job that accepts a JSONL eval set + prompt-template, runs the template against our hosted inference (batch mode), computes a small metrics report (token counts, top-k diffs, simple classifiers), stores results in a drive object, and provides a promotion toggle in the Console as a "manual promote" (no inference-time changes). No per-request runtime hooks required.

B) Deeper path (4–8 weeks): add per-account prompt-template binding at runtime so that requests for that account automatically use the selected template (this touches runtime routing, caching semantics, and rollout safety). This is more seamless but requires careful KV cache invalidation and a rollback path.

Questions for scoping:
- How large is the eval set (monica said "small") — can you confirm approximate record count and average tokens per record?
- Is CoreBank expecting the eval to run inside their dedicated environment or ok with hosted-run results?

If Monica confirms small eval and hosted run is acceptable, we can target option A as an initial canary and schedule option B for a later sprint if the customer wants runtime binding. Dev — can you weigh in on work estimates for option A? Karthik/Jasmine — any console/ops considerations?

Marissa
Director, Product Management
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Marissa —
Thanks, option A sounds perfect for the POC. Quick answers:
- Eval set attached is ~120 records, avg ~80 tokens each.
- CoreBank is OK with hosted-run results for the POC; they want the artifacts for their compliance review.

They've asked for a canary window starting the week of 3/28. If we can deliver a manual-run eval job + exported report and a Console button to promote, that's enough to unblock them. I'll commit internal engineering time from CoreBank for integration and will flag procurement if any extra security artifacts are needed.

Can we get a short plan + ETA and any known risks? I'm happy to join a 30-min sync.

—Monica

> Monica —
>
> Thanks for the clear ask and attachments. High-level thoughts: conceptually this is sensible...

Quick engineering note (option A feasibility):
- Implementation for A: a small batch-run service that pulls the JSONL, spins up a short-lived batch job against the hosted inference cluster with fixed token/seq limits, aggregates outputs and diffs, and emits a report. We already have most of this plumbing in the eval-runner microservice, so incremental work is small.
- Estimated effort: ~3 engineer-days to wire the Console button + job scheduling + report storage + access controls. We can prototype in our dev environment and run the attached eval set by 3/28 if we prioritize.
- Risks/constraints: need a signed agreement allowing CoreBank eval data to be processed in hosted infra (I see NDA attached; security may still request a data handling checklist). Also: ensure that queued batch jobs don't count as live production traffic for quota billing — sales/finance needs to confirm billing semantics for eval runs.

I'll take a spike today, will post a short implementation doc in the Drive link Marissa posted.

—Dev
